jp: 来週[らいしゅう]{の|no-possessive}日曜日[にちようび]、友達[ともだち]{と|to-with}京都[きょうと]{へ/に|e-direction}行[い]きます。
en: Next Sunday I'm going to Kyoto with a friend.
why: へ marks the direction of travel; 行く moves toward Kyoto.

jp: 夏休[なつやす]み{に|ni-time}、友達[ともだち]{は/が|wa-topic}北海道[ほっかいどう]{へ/に|e-direction}旅行[りょこう]します。
en: During the summer vacation my friend will travel to Hokkaido.
why: へ marks the direction a trip heads in, the place travelled to.

jp: 彼[かれ]{は/が|wa-topic}笑[わら]い{ながら|nagara-while}私[わたし]{の|no-possessive}ほう{へ/に|e-direction}歩[ある]いてきました。
why: へ marks the direction something moves in, here toward my side.

jp: 今度[こんど]{の|no-possessive}休[やす]み{は|wa-topic}どこ{へ/に|e-direction}行[い]きたいです{か|ka-question}。
en: Where do you want to go on the next holiday?
why: 行く takes the place it heads for with へ, even when that place is a question word.

jp: 山田[やまだ]さん{が/は|ga-subject}駅[えき]{の|no-possessive}ほう{へ/に|e-direction}手[て]{を|o-object}振[ふ]りました。
en: Mr. Yamada waved his hand toward the station.
why: へ marks the direction the waving is aimed in.

jp: 将来[しょうらい]{は|wa-topic}外国[がいこく]{へ/に|e-direction}行[い]っ{て|te-sequence}働[はたら]きたいです。
en: In the future I want to go abroad and work.
why: 行く heads toward a place, so the destination takes へ.
